Scouting Summary

Common themes

  • Right Fast, averaging 132.4 kph (up to 138.6).
  • Often takes the new ball (opens in 36% of innings).
  • Typical length is 8-9m (their good length); median 7.8 m.
  • Stock ball is a good length down the leg side, hitting the stumps (19% of deliveries).
  • Goes round the wicket 44% of the time against left-handers.
  • Round the wicket he shifts his pitching line from stumps to wide of 6th and pitches fuller, up to 7.7 m.
  • Across an over he varies his length a lot, starting shorter then pitching up through the over.

Biggest threats

  • Most dangerous length is Back of Length (4 wkts, 5.0% adjusted strike).
  • Danger pitching line: Stumps.
  • Takes 20% of wickets pitching a good length down the leg side.
  • Beats the bat 4.0% of tracked balls (false-shot 23.1%).
  • Gets you bowled more than most — 33% of his wickets (1.9× the typical rate for this type).
  • 0% of catches are behind the wicket (keeper / slips / gully).

Areas to exploit

  • Concedes most runs pitching a good length down the leg side (15% of runs).
  • Short ball: 35% of deliveries, economy 3.0 — 7 wkts from 124 short balls.
  • Away from back of length, the wicket threat drops off — look to score in the less-productive lengths.
  • Most of his runs leak straight down the ground (46%) — his main scoring release.
  • Cash in when he goes good length outside off (economy 3.5, beats the bat only 27%).
